title: Human PMS1-dependent non-canonical mismatch repair engages with MBD4 to repair methylated CpG deamination.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the Europe PMC supplementary archive: it holds 14 figure images plus one 10-page PDF (gkag771_supplemental_file.pdf, 3.39 MB) and no data tables of any kind. Read the full open-access text, data availability statement and the complete methods. Queried the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) metadata interface for study EGAS50000001662 (404 from the application programming interface; the human-readable page is a JavaScript app behind a login-gated download route) and fetched the ModelArchive entry ma-8z967 (a JavaScript page, licence Creative Commons Attribution, holding theoretical protein-structure models only).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experiment counts and the cohort description: four target cytosines total (two methylated, two unmethylated), repair read out by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction; whole-genome sequencing of a small set of HAP1 knockout subclones at 25-fold coverage; Genomics England National Genomic Research Library tumour-normal pairs analysed inside their secure environment. None of these numeric values or per-sample measurements appear in any downloadable file.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified. Every measurement this paper generated sits behind an access application: the new cell-line whole-genome sequencing is in the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGAS50000001662, controlled access via a Data Access Committee), the previously published genomes are in EGA too (EGAS50000000536, EGAD00001003568, EGAD00001005454), and the tumour cohort is only reachable inside the Genomics England secure Research Environment for approved network members. The only openly downloadable items are a 10-page supplementary PDF of figures and a handful of theoretical protein-structure models in ModelArchive (ma-8z967). No table of per-site or per-sample values exists anywhere.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified. The quantities a model would predict (percent C-to-T fractional abundance per target per genotype; per-clone mutational-signature burdens) exist only as plotted points in the figures. They would have to be reconstructed from raw sequencing reads or digitised off images.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. Sequence context for the four targets is given only as primer and guide-RNA sequences in the methods; genomic coordinates for the target cytosines are never tabulated, so inputs would need manual reconstruction against GRCh38.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clearly stated in the text (percent C-to-T fractional abundance by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction; single-base-substitution counts per genome), but there is no file carrying them.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, from the methods text. The targeted-deamination assay uses exactly four cytosine targets (methylated #1 in DNAJC16, #2 in LRP8; unmethylated #1 in STK38, #2 in HNRNPDL) across roughly six knockout genotypes with technical replicates, i.e. tens of measurements. The whole-genome sequencing arm is a few subclones per genotype. Far under the ~1,500-row bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Nothing open is large; the controlled whole-genome sequencing would be terabyte-scale raw reads, which the project rules exclude anyway.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: there are no downloadable counts to compare with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle: repair outcomes come from droplet digital polymerase chain reaction genotyping of sorted cells, and mutation burdens from GATK Mutect2 variant calls followed by signature fitting. Not another model's prediction, though the signature-burden values are themselves the output of a fitting procedure.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is available: with four assayed cytosines and no released measurement table, nothing can be trained or tested.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use local DNA sequence and chromatin context to predict whether a damaged methylated CpG site gets repaired before it becomes a mutation.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would have used each targeted cytosine site as one example, with features from surrounding DNA sequence, methylation level and chromatin accessibility. Verified count of such sites in this paper: 4.
plain_idea.predict: The fraction of DNA molecules at that site still carrying an unrepaired C-to-T change, measured by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction after targeted deamination with an APOBEC1 enzyme fused to a disabled Cas9 protein.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: DNA repair and cancer-genomics groups would like to know which methylated CpG positions in the genome are repair-resistant, since those become the mutation hotspots seen in ageing and tumours; this paper is a beautiful mechanism study but supplies four such positions, not a dataset.

ml_idea: Considered and dropped: predict per-site repair efficiency of 5-methylcytosine deamination damage (T:G mismatch) from sequence and chromatin context, with mismatch-repair and base-excision-repair genotype as a covariate. Dead on arrival because the assay covers four genomic positions and no per-site measurements are released.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; the project fails Part A before any compute question arises.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the target cytosines in the methods. It says four. That alone kills it, and it took one read of one paragraph.

verdict_reason: Mechanism paper, not a dataset. All measured data is controlled-access (European Genome-phenome Archive study EGAS50000001662 plus the Genomics England secure environment), the supplement I downloaded is a 10-page PDF of figures with zero data tables, and the central assay covers exactly four cytosine targets read out by droplet digital polymerase chain reaction. Fails A1 (access application required), A2 (labels exist only inside figures), A3 and A5 (four sites).
